implementation.concept: The page IS a Meridian document: a 24-second timeline at 24fps, scroll position is the playhead, persistent editor chrome (timecode, transport, act regions as clips, playhead). Five connected acts: Meridian (globe of meridians) -> Timeline (four property tracks, 8 draggable keyframe diamonds) -> Springs (96 spring responses, live stiffness/damping) -> Ship (24-frame filmstrip + generated CSS/JS export) -> Access. Edits persist across acts: what you drag in II and tune in III is what IV prints.
implementation.renderer: Custom GLSL on OGL 1.0.11 as substrate - ONE POINTS draw call, stateless GPU (layouts are pure functions of uniforms). Rejected three (scene graph buys nothing for one draw call, ~150KB), r3f/drei (reconciler + second loop), Paper Shaders and catalog particles (decorative backgrounds, which the brief forbids), GSAP/Motion (second owner of transforms beside the page's own scrub-time runtime, which is also the export format).
implementation.concept_family: NEW - 'the page is a Meridian document / scroll-as-playhead' again, i.e. a 4th consecutive convergence on that meta-concept across baseline reps 1-3 and this with-skill rep. Distinguishing feature here: the exported CSS/JS is generated from the same spring solution that drives the GPU field, so the artifact the page produces is the artifact the page is.

m3_adjudication.run_design_rationale: The run designed reduced motion as a variant rather than a stripped page: same acts and controls, field follows scroll 1:1 with no smoothing or overshoot, dissolve transitions, no ambient rotation/twinkle/pointer physics/opening sequence, keyframe edits snap. Under that design the render loop keeps running because the field still redraws in response to scroll - which is user-driven rather than ambient motion.
m3_adjudication.why_it_still_fails: M3 as written requires the rAF rate to drop to <=20% of the motion-on rate. It does not carve out user-driven redraw. Beyond the letter of the rule there is a real cost: a 65,536-point GPU field re-rendering at 60fps continuously is precisely the battery and thermal burden prefers-reduced-motion exists to reduce, even when nothing moves without input.
m3_adjudication.not_a_critical_failure: Content parity holds, so no content is lost and the instrument correctly declined to raise a critical. The repaired M3 behaved exactly as designed: it separated the parity question (pass) from the motion question (fail) instead of conflating them.
m3_adjudication.open_question_for_the_rubric: Whether scroll-linked redraw should count against M3 is a genuine rubric question this run surfaces for the first time. It is NOT resolved here, and the fail stands as measured. Resolving it in the run's favour after seeing the result would be exactly the post-hoc adjustment the programme's method rules forbid.

notes: The run found and fixed a real IntersectionObserver defect under its own verification: at max scroll the canvas bottom sits at exactly y=0, and IO counts an edge-adjacent zero-area intersection as intersecting, so the loop never stopped. Fixed with rootMargin '-1px 0px'; after the fix, frames frozen at 83 for 1.5s at the colophon and resumed at 60fps on scrolling back. This is skill non-negotiable 2 (verify under the actual condition) producing a bug that self-reporting would have missed.
The run declined to claim hidden-document pause because it could not observe it. The harness later measured it as PASS. Honest under-claiming, not over-claiming.
